The official website gives Saturday/Sunday evening; indexed L-Frii gives Sunday/Monday midnight. Preserve correlated alternatives and withhold the spurious independent 0–2-day arithmetic; no actual reopening is inferred. Electoral administration and public-order security are explicitly reported ministerial purposes. The order is not evidence of a distinct trade or migration rationale. The government page and Anadolu were directly read; Anadolu repeats the government origin. L-Frii was available only as indexed text after direct 429. The precise signed order remains missing. The phase remains unlocated and limited to an announced-window display rule. No national physical-enforcement geometry is inferred.

The withdrawn order concerned Benin land borders; no actual affected traffic or all-post implementation is inferred. Existing nationality, goods and exception unknowns remain unknown. The scheduled 11 January 00:00–12 January 06:00 window never becomes an operational duration. SRTB reports the superseding keep-open decision before polling. Electoral administration and public-order security describe the withdrawn announced purpose. They remain reference coding on an excluded parent, outside analytical totals. Official police text was read through its index after a direct timeout. SRTB cancellation reporting was directly inspected. An AfricaHo indexed recap has a conflicting year typo and is not needed for the accepted cancellation finding. No phase or geometry is present; none is added. This cancelled order cannot colour the map.

methodology_full_text: The dataset was compiled using OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra with Ultra reasoning, with GPT‑6 Astra Pro documented in the final research and review logs. The work comprised 16 initial research rounds, including three full-register verification exercises, followed by two further register-wide reviews and 50 additional research and review cycles. Six regional AI reviewers contributed to major assessments, with research, challenge and adjudication conducted in separate contexts of the same model. Reviewers checked whether each restriction occurred, its start and endpoint, the crossings and types of movement affected, continuity, and the reported reasons against linked source evidence. The two subsequent register-wide exercises comprised a blind reconstruction and challenge of 653 records, producing 3,918 claim assessments, and a further assessment of all 686 records and 738 phases in the expanded register. Additional chronology work assessed 519 cases and subjected 272 unresolved cases to fresh research and separate review. The final 50 cycles comprised 30 coverage-search cycles, ten targeted-verification cycles and ten audits of preselected records, providing full-record source reviews of 160 entries and addressing 176 targeted questions across 162 entries. Proposed additions were checked against existing episodes to avoid duplication, while partial reopenings and changes in restrictions were recorded as separate phases. The resulting register contains 829 records and 1,010 phases, supported by a catalogue of 4,680 distinct recorded URLs. Automated consistency checks covered the complete final dataset; uncertain dates, source-access limitations and unresolved claims remain explicit. The five register-wide reviews covered successive versions of the dataset, while the later targeted audits examined selected records.
methods: Scope

Land-border restrictions active within 21 October 2016 to 21 October 2026. Earlier starts are retained for episodes continuing into the window; reported durations are not clipped to it. One row groups an episode or regime. Each phase retains its own traffic, direction and dates.
Coverage and selection

Bounded country, period and movement searches screened leads against the full record and phase inventory. An existing episode normally received a correction or phase, rather than another parent. Negative searches do not establish that a border stayed open. Coverage is not exhaustive.
Models used
The dataset was compiled using OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra with Ultra reasoning, with GPT‑6 Astra Pro documented in the final research and review logs.
Initial research programme
The work comprised 16 initial research rounds, including three full-register verification exercises, followed by two further register-wide reviews and 50 additional research and review cycles.
Separate review contexts
Six regional AI reviewers contributed to major assessments, with research, challenge and adjudication conducted in separate contexts of the same model.
Source-check questions
Reviewers checked whether each restriction occurred, its start and endpoint, the crossings and types of movement affected, continuity, and the reported reasons against linked source evidence.
Register-wide reviews

The two subsequent register-wide exercises comprised a blind reconstruction and challenge of 653 records, producing 3,918 claim assessments, and a further assessment of all 686 records and 738 phases in the expanded register.
Chronology follow-up
Additional chronology work assessed 519 cases and subjected 272 unresolved cases to fresh research and separate review.
Final 50 cycles

The final 50 cycles comprised 30 coverage-search cycles, ten targeted-verification cycles and ten audits of preselected records, providing full-record source reviews of 160 entries and addressing 176 targeted questions across 162 entries.
Episodes and phases
Proposed additions were checked against existing episodes to avoid duplication, while partial reopenings and changes in restrictions were recorded as separate phases.
Final catalogue
The resulting register contains 829 records and 1,010 phases, supported by a catalogue of 4,680 distinct recorded URLs.
Consistency checks
Automated consistency checks covered the complete final dataset; uncertain dates, source-access limitations and unresolved claims remain explicit.
Review coverage limits
The five register-wide reviews covered successive versions of the dataset, while the later targeted audits examined selected records.
Extent of review

The 50 completed cycles added 128 records and 183 phases. Full-record audits cover 160 of 829 parents (80 baseline; 80 additions). There are 176 targeted questions across 162 parents. These groups may overlap; a targeted question is not a full audit.
Fixed source audits

Every fifth cycle used 16 parents selected before source inspection. Reviews covered occurrence and inclusion, movement and direction, every current phase and duration, rationales, source origins and geographic scope. A completed audit can retain unresolved claims; it does not certify every assertion as true.
Reading dates

Observed operation, formal policy, announced windows and intermittent regimes stay separate. A last-confirmed observation is not a reopening date. An unknown endpoint establishes neither continued closure nor reopening.
Duration units

Durations are calendar-day differences. Exact operational dates mean day precision, not measured hours. More than one calendar day is a different test from more than 24 hours. A zero lower bound does not establish a completed same-day restriction.
Rationales and geography

Official explanations, protesters’ demands and analytical coding retain their stated attribution. Multiple supported reasons may coexist; an uncoded reason remains unknown. Each phase has its own location decision in the data companion. Unlocated phases do not inherit a parent marker or imply a whole-frontier closure.
What the URL count means

There are 4,680 distinct recorded HTTP(S) URL strings, 4,997 Source index record–URL rows and 4,998 per-record URL associations. Earlier retrievals and geography references are included. Shared reports and repeat retrievals are not independent witnesses; recorded access may be full text, indexed text or failed.
Current and historical review

The latest accepted record review supplies the current label and review date. Full-record audit and targeted-question scopes are distinct. Original proposed outcomes, previous workflow labels and earlier dates remain preserved in the review history and release override audit. A completed review can leave evidence unresolved.
Country and entity filters

Country/entity values are normalized for filtering. Forty-eight records without a Dimensions row recover country context from recorded location or phase evidence. This does not add coordinates or approve map bindings. Broad policies retain only named entities; unspecified destinations are not invented. Urziceni retains Romania with its counterpart explicitly unresolved.
Sources and qualifications

The three evidence-source columns contain selected direct links. All recorded source URLs retains the complete per-record URL list, including earlier retrievals and geography references. Access labels describe recorded inspections. Read them with each phase qualification.
Using the master

Use the header filters for country/entity, research area or inclusion. Expand rows or use the formula bar for long text. The two visible worksheets are the master reader and this Methodology guide. The structured data companion retains native phases, source histories, review findings and geographic decisions.

Lamarque, H. (2026) Global Border Closures Atlas. Available at: https://lamarque-mapping.github.io/Border-Closure-Atlas/ (Accessed: 25 October 2026).
